title: Selling Plans — Order-Size Caps on Chargeback Administration Fees
content:
On **Selling Plans**, the cap that holds down the administration fee withheld from a chargeback credit is set by the size of the charged-back order, measured by the fee basis shown on its variable final value fee record.

**Rule.** The chargeback administration fee cap is the large-order chargeback cap when the order's fee basis is at least the large-order basis, the mid-order chargeback cap when it is at least the mid-order basis but below the large-order basis, and the refund administration fee cap below the mid-order basis.

| Fee basis of the charged-back order | Chargeback administration fee cap |
|---|---|
| USD 1000.00 or more (the large-order basis) | USD 10.00 (large-order chargeback cap) |
| USD 250.00 or more but below USD 1000.00 (the mid-order basis up to the large) | USD 7.50 (mid-order chargeback cap) |
| Below USD 250.00 | The plan's refund administration fee cap |

## Both sides of each threshold (hypothetical orders)

- Fee basis USD 1000.00 → cap USD 10.00; USD 999.99 → cap USD 7.50.
- Fee basis USD 250.00 → cap USD 7.50; USD 249.99 → the plan's refund administration fee cap.

**Holding a fee to the cap (hypothetical).** An administration fee worked out at USD 12.40 on an order with a fee basis of USD 1200.00 is held to USD 10.00; one worked out at USD 6.10 on an order with a fee basis of USD 300.00 stays at USD 6.10, under the USD 7.50 cap.
